$comment: Milestone 3 map measurements after the M3 review fixes (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §14: map moveend redraw at the LOD cap <= 16 ms, one route edit applied <= 8 ms; docs/MAPS.md §7.2-§7.5; docs/UI.md §12). They replace the pre-review figures of 2026-09-25, which the review showed understated a 10,000-step route edit about 3x (they came from a fake adapter; M3 review PERF-2). Those are kept under 'beforeReview' for comparison.

browser: the real map controller (src/app/map-controller.ts), the real Leaflet adapter (src/map/leaflet) and the committed dataset (loadWorkspace over public/data), driven from the page with no React, in a 1280x800 host (DPR 1, the pane's Chrome 152) on the Vite dev server (sources as modules, not minified: the controller and adapter are not React code, so dev mode changes their cost little). The pane was hidden, so requestAnimationFrame never ran: after each action the canvas renderer was redrawn by calling its _redraw() once ('redrawForced'); 'handler' is the synchronous time of the action (store dispatch or select, the controller's sync, the adapter's setLayer and moveend work), 'sync' the frl:map:sync User Timing measure (recorded only when a layer is set), 'setLayer' the adapter's frl:map:set-layer measures, 'updatePaths' frl:map:update-paths. 11 to 15 runs per case, min / median / max.

Load: other processes kept the machine busy (other agents' builds and two long-running Vite dev servers from earlier sessions; system CPU 35-98% while measuring). A hidden tab runs at background priority, so browser figures moved by 2-4x with the load: runs at 97% CPU gave 45 ms for the same 10,000-step selection change that took 12-17 ms when the load was lower. The browser figures below come from the calmer runs, checked with a CPU probe (2e7 sqrt loop: 40 ms in the page, 40 ms in Node at that time). Treat them as indicative; the throttled Playwright run of Milestone 9 replaces them.

node: the same controller and map/layers over the same committed dataset (loadWorkspace through the test fake fetch, tests/support/fake-fetch.ts), with the fake adapter of src/app/map-test-helpers.ts (records calls, no Leaflet, no canvas), 21 runs per case, tsx on Node v22.13.1, a foreground process. It isolates the app and map/layers cost; the browser rows give the adapter's setLayer and redraw on top. 'storeOnly' is the same dispatch on a store without a map, so the map's share is total - storeOnly.

The 10,000-step route repeats the sample's 55 steps with each repeat's zone percentages shifted by up to 1.5 (so markers do not all stack; about 3,456 step markers remain after merging, 700 drawn under the step-marker budget). All of it lies in Durotar and the Valley of Trials: the densest possible case for the step-marker cap.

Scenarios: insert a note at spread positions; edit a note's text; move a placed step by one (it is selected and active first, outside the measurement); a selection change as the shell makes it (store.select, then controller.setActiveStep with the same step, which now changes nothing: one sync, M3 review PERF-6); pans of 120 px and 700 px at zone zoom with the cap biting; jump to zone on a 424x634 stage (1366x768 with the layer panel open), where The Barrens would fit only at zoom -5 and Durotar at -4 without the zoom floor.

$comment: Milestone 4 re-measure of the M3 review's known issue PERF-2 (docs/reviews/review-m3-map.md): the step-marker layer's cache key included the focus, so a selection change rebuilt all 10,000 steps, and a route edit did too. The fix (src/map/layers.ts): route-steps no longer sees the focus (every marker 'normal'; the selection layer draws the focused steps' halos and a strong copy of their markers, the active step's first under its cap), and it is built from caches: a candidate per step input (with its occurrence and leg flag), each candidate's point interned as a small integer so stacks are found with a typed-array count, and merged stacks by their members. The controller asks the route input builder whether a focused step is drawn instead of building a set of every drawn id (src/app/map-controller.ts, map-model.ts).

node: tests/bench/map-edit.bench.ts (M4 review CR-07), `pnpm exec tsx tests/bench/map-edit.bench.ts`: the real map controller and map/layers over the committed dataset (loadWorkspace through tests/support/fake-fetch.ts), the fake adapter of src/app/map-test-helpers.ts, tsx on Node v22.13.1, a foreground process, 21 runs per case after 3 warm-ups, min / median / p90. The 10,000-step route: the sample's 55 steps repeated, each repeat shifted by up to 1.5 zone percent; the view at zone zoom (-2) over Durotar, the cap biting. 'storeOnly' is the same store change on a store without a map, so the map's share is total - storeOnly. Two runs agreed within 0.2 ms; the rows are the second. With `--check docs/measurements/map-m3.json` the script compares its route medians with 'route10000' below and exits with 1 on a regression over 25% (ARCHITECTURE §14). The first Milestone 4 figures, from the engineer's uncommitted script with the same scenarios, were 2.29 / 6.26 / 3.61 / 2.24 ms median (selection change, move, insert note, edit note).

browser ('browserRoute10000'): re-measured as the M3 'browser' rows were, with the real Leaflet adapter (src/map/leaflet) under the real controller and the committed dataset, driven from the page with no React in a 1280x800 host, on the Vite dev server (sources as modules, not minified), in the Claude desktop app's built-in browser (Chrome 152) with its pane hidden, so requestAnimationFrame never ran: after each action the canvas renderer was redrawn once by calling its _redraw() ('redrawForced'); 'handler' is the synchronous time of the action (store change, the controller's sync, the adapter's setLayer), 'handlerPlusRedraw' the two together, 'sync' and 'setLayer' the frl:map:sync and frl:map:set-layer User Timing measures (medians). 21 runs per case after 3 warm-ups, each in its own task; two runs, [first, second]. The machine was calm: the CPU probe (2e7 sqrt loop) took 39-40 ms in the page and 38-40 ms in Node. A production build was not measured: its bundled modules cannot be driven from the page this way.

Scenarios: selection change = store.select of a placed step then controller.setActiveStep with it, as the shell does (the map follows the step, so a pan to another ranking cell can still re-rank the step markers: that is a view change, not the selection); move = moveSelected by one (alternately down and up) of a placed, selected and active step, the middle of the placed steps; insert note at spread positions; edit a step's note. Note inserts and edits set no layer, so their forced redraw is a full redraw that the page itself would not do.

parts.$comment: one 10,000-step move, timed piece by piece (median of 55): route-steps went from 7.4 ms (focus-free but uncached) to 3.8 ms (candidate and stack caches) to 1.4 ms (interned points instead of a map keyed by coordinates)

milestone4Perf2.verdict: Much faster, but not shown to be within budget. Node (the committed bench): a 10,000-step move 5.0 ms median (5.6 ms p90), was 14.8 ms; a selection change 1.8 ms (2.3 ms p90), was 12.2 ms; the selection change no longer sends the step-marker layer. Browser, unthrottled, with the real adapter: a move applies in 5.5-5.9 ms median (p90 6.4-7.9 ms), 6.0-6.8 ms median with its canvas redraw (p90 7.2-8.7 ms, max 9.1 ms); a selection change 3.5-4.7 ms (5.6-5.9 ms with the redraw, p90 7.9-9.2 ms). So an unthrottled median edit fits the 8 ms budget and its slowest tenth does not always; under the 4x CPU throttle ARCHITECTURE §14 prescribes for the browser, the same work would take roughly four times as long. PERF-2 is therefore not closed on these figures: the known issue stays open (with them) until the throttled Playwright run of Milestone 9.

verdict: Sample route: well within both budgets (a route edit 0.3-1 ms, a selection change about 3 ms, a pan 4-5 ms with its redraw).
10,000 steps, note edits: within budget (inserting or editing a note costs 2.6-4 ms, most of it the store's own dispatch; no route layer is rebuilt).

10,000 steps, moving a placed step or changing the selection: over the 8 ms budget at Milestone 3 (13-17 ms in Node, 15-20 ms in the browser when the machine was calmer). The app's own share is about 1 ms (route input 0.5 ms, route summary 0.2 ms); most of the rest is map/layers routeSteps rebuilding all 10,000 steps on any route or focus change (reported to the map core). One selection change is now one sync, where it was two. Milestone 4 (PERF-2) cut a move to 5.0 ms and a selection change to 1.8 ms median in Node, and a move to 6.0-6.8 ms median with its redraw in the unthrottled browser (p90 up to 8.7 ms): see 'milestone4Perf2'. Not closed until the 4x-throttled run of Milestone 9.
Pans: within the 16 ms budget at 1,348 paths (4-5 ms with the redraw); a surface at the full 2,500-path cap is measured in MAPS §7.2 (standalone harness, 3.3-3.5 ms median update-paths).

beforeReview.$comment: 2026-09-25, before the M3 review fixes. browser: production build, sample route; node: the fake adapter as above but a 10,000-step route of exact repeats, labels in descriptors, and two syncs per selection change.

reviewBrowser10000.$comment: the M3 render review (PERF-2), real adapter

$comment: Map route edit with walking paths (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §14: one route edit applied, 8 ms), stored at the final verification after the Milestone 6 and 3b.6 fix pass (2026-09-26). First stored baseline: the review fixes rebuilt the path feed (NAV-06, NAV-07, NAV-09, PERF-09) and the bench gained --budget and --check.

Script: pnpm exec tsx tests/bench/map-paths.bench.ts --budget (21 runs after 3 warm-ups); median is the median of three processes' medians (runMedians). `--check <file>` reads paths10000.<case>.median and fails on more than 25% over it.
